opportunities.title: Harmony Is Deleting 109,000 Transactions to Undo One Hack — Ask Yourself What 'Immutable' Actually Means Now
opportunities.why_now: A chain is about to unilaterally erase over 100k transactions to reverse a single exploit, reopening the 'code is law' debate in real time.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/opinion: walk through the rollback mechanics, compare to DAO fork precedent, and argue this is the quiet part said loud — chains will rewrite history when insiders are exposed, not when users are.

opportunities.title: DefiLlama Delayed Its Own App Because Apple's Store Was Full of Fake DefiLlama Apps
opportunities.why_now: A top DeFi data provider just admitted phishing clones beat them to launch on Apple's supposedly curated store.
opportunities.angle: Security explainer: how App Store phishing clones work, why 'official app store' is not a security boundary, checklist for verifying any crypto app before download.

opportunities.title: BitMart's Founder Won't Allow an Audit While Users Report Frozen Funds — We've Seen This Movie Before
opportunities.why_now: Real-time reports of blocked withdrawals and unpaid staff plus a founder publicly refusing an audit is the exact sequence that preceded FTX, Celsius, and a dozen others.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition piece: lay out the 'audit refusal → withdrawal freeze → silence' playbook with past exchange collapses as a timeline, ending on what to do with funds now, not later.

opportunities.title: The $165M 'Crypto Program' Ponzi Just Got Its Promoter Deported From Fiji — The Red Flags Were All Public
opportunities.why_now: A newly confirmed $165M Ponzi promoter's deportation gives a concrete, resolved case study while memories of the scheme's marketing are still fresh.
opportunities.angle: Post-mortem/checklist: reconstruct the promoter's public claims and yield promises, map them to standard Ponzi tells, and turn it into a reusable red-flag list for spotting the next one before it hits $165M.

opportunities.title: Bitpanda Just Ate Europe's First MiCA Fine — Here's What It Actually Signals for Every Exchange Operating Under 'Compliant' Licenses
opportunities.why_now: This is the first published MiCA penalty in the EU, turning theoretical regulatory risk into a concrete enforcement precedent.
opportunities.angle: Analysis: decode what triggered the fine, why 'MiCA-licensed' has been treated as a safety signal by users, and what this means for trusting license badges going forward.
